sections.h2: Which Southfield offices send the bill and set the value?
sections.html:
The City of Southfield bills and collects its own property tax, and its Treasurer's Office sits in the City Hall Municipal Complex at 26000 Evergreen Road. The counter takes payments each weekday from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. Southfield lies in Oakland County, and the county treasurer inherits whatever the city has not collected once its own window closes.

A second office sets values. Assessing counts every parcel as it stood on Tax Day, December 31, and aims each assessment at half of fair market value, drawing on site visits, recorded transfers and a two-year sales study. Disputes are heard in March by the Board of Review.

Pick the right phone line. Treasurer, (248) 796-5200: due dates, payment methods, deferments, special assessments, millage. Assessing, (248) 796-5230: a value, a parcel number, an exemption, a new mailing address.

sections.h2: When are Southfield summer and winter taxes due?
sections.html:
Summer bills are payable July 1 through August 31 without penalty, and winter bills run December 1 to February 14. Southfield publishes each one as a payment window, so the closing day of the window is the deadline.

Southfield payment windows and penalties, from the city Treasurer's Office FAQ and 2026 summer legal notice
BillPay without penaltyFirst penaltyAfter the city period
SummerJuly 1 through August 313.5% added on September 1, then one-half of 1% on October 1 and each month afterOakland County Treasurer adds a 4% collection fee and 1% interest per month
WinterDecember 1 through February 143% added on February 15Payable only to the Oakland County Treasurer after February 28

The 2026 summer notice names March 1, 2027 as the point after which payment goes only to the county. Mailed payments need a USPS postmark no later than the due date, and the city does not accept metered postmarks. The city says state law bars extensions for hardship or any other reason. It does take partial payments, with penalties and interest running on the rest.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Southfield property tax bill?
sections.html:
Five routes exist, and the cost differs by route.

  • At the Treasurer's counter with a check, cash or money order.
  • By post to the City of Southfield Treasurer's Office at the Evergreen Road address, with the parcel number written on the check and the envelope.
  • On the city's payment site by card or electronic check, which adds 2.3% with a $1.95 floor. Looking up your taxes costs nothing.
  • Over the phone at (833) 505-4394, priced like the web payment.
  • Through the round-the-clock drop box beside the main door on the circular drive facing Evergreen Road. It will not take cash.

You can pay without the printed bill if you know the amount, as long as the check carries the parcel ID and your phone number. Lenders that escrow tax get the bill in your place. When you pay on your own and no summer bill has arrived by July 1, ask the Treasurer for a copy.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Southfield tax?
sections.html:
Once the city window closes, unpaid tax is handed to Oakland County and the cost climbs. The city's tax page states that delinquent tax and earlier-year tax now belong to the county treasurer in Pontiac, reachable at (248) 858-0611.

The county's fee is 4%, with 1% interest each month. Southfield also links a Delinquent Tax Timeline and a way to pay the county in cash at a 7-Eleven store. An owner who is behind and wants to sell should request a written payoff before choosing a closing date, since the number moves monthly.

sections.h2: What exemptions and relief does Southfield offer?
sections.html:
Southfield lists three exemptions on its Assessing page and a deferment through the Treasurer. Each has its own form and proof requirements.

  • Principal Residence Exemption: owners who claim a house as their principal residence do not pay the school operating mills on the bill.
  • Hardship exemption: residents below Southfield's poverty guidelines may qualify, and the application sits on the Forms page under Assessment Resources.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: a VA disability rating of 100% or more, or a declared unemployable status, may qualify. The claim needs the annual VA Summary of Benefits letter, DD214, VA identification card and driver's license.
  • Summer tax deferment: for owner-residents with income up to $40,000 who are 62 or older, or retired because of a disability. Applications are taken only between July 1 and September 15.

The Assessing Department accepts real property transfers and exemption forms by email at contactassessing@cityofsouthfield.com, but every submission needs an original signature. Appointments with staff are booked through the Contact Staff page.

sections.h2: What should I know about Southfield before selling a house here?
sections.html:
Eight Mile Road forms Southfield's southern edge, shared with Detroit, and Greenfield Road marks the east, inside about 26 square miles of land. The city was incorporated on April 28, 1958, after starting as Southfield Township in 1830, and the Rouge River runs through it. The separate city of Lathrup Village sits as an enclave inside its eastern side.

Office towers anchor the economy: about 27 million square feet, behind only downtown Detroit in the metro area. Southfield City Centre sits at the I-696 and Lodge Freeway (M-10) crossing, with the Southfield Freeway (M-39) and Telegraph Road (US 24) also running through. Southfield Public Schools runs a single high school, Southfield A&T, while the northern edge sends students to Birmingham schools and the southeast corner to Oak Park schools.

Southfield counts 34,860 households in the 2020 to 2024 Census Bureau survey, and just over half (53.4%) own. Typical owner-occupied value reads $236,200, gross rent $1,340, and monthly owner costs $1,779 with a mortgage against $764 without.

sections.h2: What tax steps come with selling a Southfield home?
sections.html:
Have the title company get a current tax status from the Treasurer ahead of closing. Southfield's online inquiry system shows assessment and tax data free of charge, though the Treasurer should confirm special assessments such as alarm billing or lawn mowing charges that a recent statement may omit.

Both sides then have paperwork. The Assessing Department takes real property transfers and exemption forms, so ask it which forms the buyer and the seller each owe for your parcel. Change of mailing address requests go to the Assessing Office in writing with the parcel number, a signature and the old and new addresses, and no deed copy is required for a mailing change alone.

Nothing forces you to clear a balance before listing. Get the amount due on the parcel from the Treasurer and let the title company pay it out of proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When does Southfield summer tax become late?
faqs.a: Summer tax becomes late after August 31. Southfield adds 3.5% on September 1, then one-half of 1% on the first day of October and each month after that until the balance moves to Oakland County.

faqs.q: Which Southfield office answers value questions?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer's Office at (248) 796-5200 for bills, due dates and deferments. Call the Assessing Department at (248) 796-5230 for values, parcel numbers and exemptions.

faqs.q: Can Southfield give me more time to pay?
faqs.a: No extension is available for hardship or other reasons, because state law governs Michigan cities. Partial payments are taken, with penalties and interest on the rest, and seniors or disabled owners who qualify can apply for a summer deferment from July 1 to September 15.

faqs.q: Where does a Southfield bill go once the county has it?
faqs.a: Pay the Oakland County Treasurer in Pontiac, and call (248) 858-0611 for the amount. The county adds a 4% collection fee plus 1% interest a month.

faqs.q: How do I claim the Principal Residence Exemption on a Southfield house?
faqs.a: File the exemption claim with the Southfield Assessing Department and sign it with an original signature. Approved owners do not pay the school operating mills portion of the tax bill.
